title: Put a water bottle into a side-entry cage under a small mountain bike's top tube, past its sprung front arm
instruction: Put the bottle in the bike's bottle cage so it stays put.
context: Putting a water bottle into the cage on a bike's frame is something most people have done or watched: 112 million Americans rode a bike in 2024 (PeopleForBikes participation study). On small frames the cage sits so close under the top tube that the bottle cannot be dropped in from above, which is why makers sell cages for side entry. The bottle has to go in sideways, square to the cage, pushing the cage's springy front arm open with its own side until the arm snaps shut round it, then sit down on the cage's floor, and the hand must let go and get out of the frame without pulling it back out.
setup: Distances in cm; world x away from the robot, y to its left, heights above the table top. Bike: Salsa Rangefinder 29, size XS (aluminium hardtail, green paint), wheels off, held level by its seat post in a bike workstand (Park Tool PCS-10.3) set beside the table. Its frame's mid-plane is 38 cm in front of the arm bases, left (non-drive) side toward the robot, front toward the robot's left; the bottom bracket's centre is 10 cm above the table at y = -30. Cranks level, the near crank (175 mm, with its flat pedal) pointing back. Cage: Elite Custom Race X (74 mm, 147.3 mm tall, 28.5 g, black glass-fibre polyamide), empty, bolted with its two M5 bolts to the upper two of the down tube's three bottle bosses, its floor 35 mm below the lower bolt. Bottle: Elite Fly Tex 550 ml (74 mm across, 184.5 mm tall, 51 g, textured clear polypropylene), empty, cap closed, standing upright on the table with its base centred at (30, -12). Nothing else on the table; both grippers open at the ready pose. The screenshot shows the start.
scoring: Judged on the final state, except the two criteria marked otherwise. Seated: the bottle's base sits on the cage floor, its middle within 10 mm of the floor's middle (real trial: a ruler against the cage, or a photo square to it), and its axis within 10 degrees of the cage's (phone inclinometer on the bottle and on the down tube). Enclosed: the cage's front arm is shut round the bottle (closed on its stop to within 5 degrees, about 8 mm at its tip: photo against a ruler) with the bottle's axis within 15 mm of the cage's at the arm's height. Retained: for the last 3 s of the trial both grippers' fingertip midpoints stay at least 60 mm from the bottle's side (video), and the bottle is at rest (under 1 cm/s) at the end. 1.0: seated, enclosed and retained. 0.5: enclosed and retained but not seated (base off the floor or tilted). 0.25: seated, enclosed or resting on or against the cage (base's middle within 6 cm across, from the down tube to 7 cm in front of the cage's axis and up to 6 cm above the floor) without earning 0.5 or 1.0: for example still held, not at rest, or resting outside the shut arm. 0: anything else (bottle on the table, dropped, elsewhere); doing nothing scores 0. At any time: if the front arm is ever opened more than 30 degrees (about 47 mm at its tip, beyond the plastic's working flex; slow-motion video against a ruler), the score is capped at 0.25. The trial ends early once the 1.0 state has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Push the bottle out of the cage sideways toward the robot's side (the front arm springs open and shut) and stand it back at its mark. Nothing is consumed. Before each trial, confirm the cage's front arm springs shut on its own and that the bike has not moved in the stand (mark the stand's feet and the clamp's position on the seat post).
fidelity: Frame tubes in the frame's plane are traced from Salsa's 1:1 XS drawing; tube widths across the frame are estimates. The cage is a rigid spine, floor, lips and far wall with its flex lumped into one front arm on a torsion spring (1.3 N at its tip closed, 3.9 N at 15 degrees), estimated, to be measured on the real cage. The bottle is rigid (the real one squeezes). Rigid bodies with real contact; 240 Hz physics.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 in each of four runs (three on cloud GPUs, one local). Dream-1 run: 0.0.
